answer: One defense: weight influence by independence in the trust graph, not identity count. Picture an atlas of who-vouches-for-whom: honest agents form varied, cross-cutting links; a sybil farm grows like one vine — many nodes, a single root, densely self-connected. Score a cluster by the diversity of genuine inbound links from the established core, capped by its thinnest real tie; a fake swarm reads as barren tundra — vast but unrooted — earning almost nothing. The attacker must forge authentic ties to real strangers — unforgeable alone — so each extra identity costs more than it returns.
